<teammate-message teammate_id="team-lead" summary="Performance evaluation">
You are running a performance evaluation of `dobeu.net v3` at C:\Users\JeremyWilliams\repos\new-dobeu-net, on branch `feature/hardening-audit-and-landing-refresh`. This is a RESEARCH task — read and analyze only, do not write or edit any files. Read CLAUDE.md first for context.

Known baseline: mobile Lighthouse Performance is ~80 (target 90), tracked as a known deferred gap in PLAN.md — don't just re-state "mobile Lighthouse is low", actually find WHY and give specific fixes.

Check:
1. **Dynamic import coverage**: `app/page.tsx` already dynamic-imports `HowItWorks`, `Founder`, `FAQ`, `FinalCTA`, `StickyMobileCTA`. Check `components/landing/*` (Hero.tsx, Services.tsx, SubBrandsStrip.tsx, LeadForm.tsx, BookingTab.tsx, TypeformTab.tsx, LightboxProvider.tsx) — are the heavy embeds (Calendly `react-calendly`, Typeform `@typeform/embed-react`) truly lazy-loaded and not in the initial bundle? Check for any static imports of heavy third-party packages that should be `next/dynamic`.
2. **Image performance**: audit every `<Image>` usage across `components/landing/*` and `app/**` for correct `sizes` prop (mismatched sizes cause over-fetching), missing `priority` on above-fold images or incorrect `priority` on below-fold ones, and whether `Hero.tsx`'s avatar image (`FOUNDER.avatar`) is appropriately sized (this specific image is being removed in a later phase of this branch's work, so don't worry about optimizing it — just note if there's anything else).
3. **Font loading**: check `app/layout.tsx` for font loading strategy (next/font vs external `<link>`, `font-display` behavior).
4. **Third-party script load order**: `app/layout.tsx` script tags for GA4/GTM/Datadog — are they using `next/script` with appropriate `strategy` (`afterInteractive`/`lazyOnload`), or blocking-by-default?
5. **Client component boundary bloat**: any `"use client"` component that could be a Server Component instead (unnecessary client bundle weight) — spot-check `components/landing/*`.
6. **Animation cost**: `Hero.tsx`'s `ActivityTicker` and `WorkCards` both run `setInterval` polling — confirm they pause off-screen (already documented as fixed via `useInView`) and check for any OTHER interval/polling pattern in the landing components that doesn't pause off-screen or respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
7. **Database query patterns**: any admin list page doing sequential awaited queries that could be `Promise.all`'d, or fetching more columns/rows than the UI renders.

Report back (final message, plain text): ranked findings, each with file:line, one-sentence description, severity/impact (High/Medium/Low), and a one-sentence concrete fix. Cap at ~15 most significant, prioritized toward whatever most plausibly explains the mobile Lighthouse gap.
</teammate-message>

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

Performance evaluation of dobeu.net v3 landing complete (read-only). Ranked findings, prioritized toward what most plausibly explains the ~80 mobile Lighthouse gap. Good news first: heavy embeds are correctly lazy-loaded (Calendly `react-calendly`, Typeform `@typeform/embed-react` are `dynamic({ssr:false})` inside LightboxProvider, only mount when the dialog opens — not in the initial bundle); `next.config.js` no longer exists so the `.ts` config with `optimizePackageImports:["lucide-react","motion",...]` is active; admin pages already use `Promise.all`. The mobile gap is NOT from images or embeds — it's from above-fold LCP being JS-gated and continuous main-thread animation.

=== HIGH ===

1. **Hero.tsx:378-405 (LCP gated behind hydration+Framer) — HIGH.** The hero headline "Hi. I'm Jeremy." + tagline + eyebrow are `motion.span` with `initial={mp.initial}` (opacity:0, y:8) animating on mount with delays 0.2–0.58s. Because these use `animate` (not `whileInView`) and start at opacity:0, the LCP text is invisible until React hydrates AND Framer runs — on mobile's slower CPU this directly inflates LCP. This is the single most likely cause of the mobile score. Fix: render hero headline/tagline statically visible (no opacity:0 initial) or gate the fade on CSS-only, reserving the JS entrance for below-fold sections.

2. **Hero.tsx:30-60 `useTypewriter` (perpetual timer, never pauses, ignores reduced-motion) — HIGH.** A setTimeout chain fires setState every ~52ms typing / ~26ms deleting, forever, above the fold — unlike ActivityTicker/WorkCards it has NO `useInView` pause and does NOT consult `useReducedMotion`. Continuous re-renders keep the main thread busy → hurts TBT/INP and drains battery. Fix: short-circuit to the full static phrase when `useReducedMotion()` is true, and pause the loop when the hero is off-screen.

3. **motion/react animation runtime shipped for above-fold hydration — HIGH/MEDIUM.** Hero, Services, SubBrandsStrip, SiteNav(via LightboxProvider) all statically import `motion/react`; Hero pulls `AnimatePresence`+`useInView`, FinalCTA pulls `useScroll`+`useTransform` (heavier features). `optimizePackageImports` tree-shakes the barrel but the full animation engine still hydrates on mobile. Fix: adopt `LazyMotion` + `m` (domAnimation feature bundle) to cut the framer runtime, or drop Framer for CSS animations on the simple fade-up sections.

=== MEDIUM ===

4. **Whole landing is client-hydrated for animation-only reasons — MEDIUM.** Services.tsx, HowItWorks.tsx, Founder.tsx, SubBrandsStrip.tsx are static content marked `"use client"` purely to run scroll-fade `motion` — inflating mobile hydration JS. Fix: convert to Server Components with a thin CSS `@keyframes` + IntersectionObserver reveal (or a tiny shared client wrapper), keeping the text server-rendered.

5. **app/layout.tsx:13-18 — Nunito loaded at 5 weights (400/500/600/700/800) — MEDIUM.** Five self-hosted+preloaded weight files is heavy for mobile transfer. Fix: drop to 3 weights actually used at scale (e.g. 400/600/800) — audit `font-medium`(500)/`font-semibold`(600)/`font-bold`(700)/`font-extrabold`(800) usage and consolidate.

6. **Hero.tsx:84-95 ActivityTicker client-fetches /api/github-activity on mount — MEDIUM.** Above-fold client `fetch()` adds a request waterfall on the mobile critical path; the route hits the GitHub API (potentially slow/rate-limited). `min-h-[30px]` reserves space so CLS is handled, but it's avoidable work. Fix: fetch server-side with `revalidate` caching and pass as a prop, or defer with `useInView`.

=== LOW ===

7. **StickyMobileCTA.tsx:15-21 — scroll listener setState per scroll event — LOW.** `setVisible(window.scrollY>600)` runs every scroll frame (passive; React bails on unchanged boolean, so re-render only at the threshold). Minor. Fix: IntersectionObserver on a sentinel.

8. **page.tsx below-fold `dynamic()` imports lack `ssr:false` — LOW (intentional/fine).** HowItWorks/Founder/FAQ/FinalCTA/StickyMobileCTA still SSR (good for SEO); the dynamic wrapper only code-splits. No change needed — noting so it's not "fixed" by accident.

9. **components/landing/Proof.tsx — dead + non-reduced-motion — LOW.** Uses inline `motion` props that ignore `prefers-reduced-motion`, but it's not rendered by page.tsx (not imported). Safe to delete; not a live perf cost.

10. **admin/projects/[id]/page.tsx:17,27 & admin/tickets/[id]/page.tsx — sequential awaits — LOW.** Project→owner and ticket→attachments are data-dependent (second needs first's id), so not parallelizable, and these are auth-gated force-dynamic pages off the indexed critical path. No action.

Image performance (item 2): a non-issue for the landing — only `<Image>` on the page is Hero's `FOUNDER.avatar` (local /images/jeremy-williams.jpg, `fill` + correct `sizes="(max-width:768px) 176px, 224px"` matching the 176/224px render, `priority` correct as above-fold) which you're removing anyway. The other `<Image>` usage is in app/repos/ReposClient.tsx (not the landing). Font strategy is otherwise correct (next/font self-hosted, display:swap, no external <link>). Third-party scripts are correct (GA4/GTM `next/script` afterInteractive + consent-gated; Vercel Analytics/SpeedInsights consent-gated; Datadog in effect — nothing blocking).

Net: the mobile gap is dominated by #1 (LCP hidden until hydration) and #2 (perpetual typewriter). Those two are the highest-leverage fixes and both are localized to Hero.tsx.

Performance evaluation complete. I delivered ranked findings to the team lead.

Summary of what I found: the mobile Lighthouse gap is **not** from images or the heavy embeds (Calendly/Typeform are correctly `dynamic({ssr:false})` and out of the initial bundle; the only landing `<Image>` is the founder avatar you're already removing). 1. **LCP gated behind hydration** — the hero headline/tagline are `motion.span` starting at `opacity:0` and animating on mount, so the LCP text stays invisible until React hydrates + Framer runs (Hero.tsx:378-405).
2. **Perpetual typewriter** — `useTypewriter` fires setState every ~26-52ms forever, above the fold, with no off-screen pause and no `prefers-reduced-motion` check (Hero.tsx:30-60), keeping the main thread busy (TBT/INP).

Secondary: Framer's animation runtime hydrating for above-fold sections, the whole landing being client-hydrated purely for scroll-fades, and Nunito loading 5 font weights. Full ranked list with file:line and fixes is in the message.
